item.title: Correction · The owner identified that DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (formerly tracked as status.csv blklot 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (formerly blklot 8722063) byte-identical geometry -- one shared master-condominium-association land parcel spanning the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (confirmed: Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). This made the two records' polygons fully overlapping on the map -- a click anywhere in the shared area could resolve to either record, and each record's own "Where it is" mini-map showed the wrong footprint. Migrated both records off status.csv onto hand-derived, non-overlapping real geometry: Chase Center (record_id mission_bay_chase_center) is now the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints subtracted out; Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (record_id mission_bay_uber_3_4) is now the union of those same two real OSM footprints. The owner also identified that Harmonic Brewing's own standalone taproom building, at the NE edge of the site (7 Warriors Way Ste 206 per its DataSF business-registration address; the registry's geocode puts Harmonic Brewing, Miller & Lux and Cupcakin' at the same point, so it does not place any of them in a particular building), and Miller & Lux (7 Warriors Way Ste 208 per its registration address; its position inside the arena footprint is not established by the registry) are both Chase Center/Thrive City tenants, not separate structures -- Harmonic Brewing's building is included in Chase Center's new geometry (it falls within the parcel-minus-Uber-towers remainder) rather than tracked as a separate record. Re-running the retail spatial join (src/join_retail.py) against the corrected geometry surfaced three more Thrive City business registrations -- Cupcakin' Bake Shop (Ste 200), 'Siren SF' (1 Warriors Way Unit 24, shown as Siren Cafe & Bar) and The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way) -- registrations at Chase Center addresses, not proof of open storefronts; see those rows; see those changelog rows.

item.title: Correction · Blocks 18B/18C corrected: independently verified a secondhand report that UCSF's own June 2025 CAC presentation (campus map updated December 2024) renumbers this block row. Cross-checking against it showed the building already tracked as '18B' (a real UCSF building complex west of Sandler Neurosciences Center, corrected 2026-09-20) is UCSF's own 'Block 18C', labeled 'Open Space (Near term: Childcare Center)'. The owner identified it directly as the existing UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center (727 Nelson Rising Lane, operating since 2006) -- renamed 18B to 18C, geometry unchanged, status changed to existing/interim ahead of a long-term open-space redesignation. With 18C's identity established, the 18A parking lot was extended east (~1,197 sqm) to close the access-lane gap that used to separate it from 18C, then re-split into new 18A/18B by an equal-area bisection so the row now runs 18A/18B (parking) back-to-back with 18C (existing childcare building). The childcare-center identification is the owner's own on-the-ground read, not independently confirmed by any source checked in this pass -- flagged as such in the record. Accuracy audit 2026-09 (2026-09-29) note: the UCSF deck cited (Dec 2024 map) lists Block 18C among 'undeveloped parcels remaining' with 'Open Space (Near term: Childcare Center)', which does not by itself show an existing building; no source read gives the 727 Nelson Rising Lane address or a 2006 start. The existing/interim status therefore rests on the owner's on-the-ground read alone and needs a source.

item.title: Correction · Block 21 split into 21A/21B: cross-checking UCSF's own June 2025 CAC presentation (campus map updated December 2024) showed the 1625 Owens St parking lot and adjoining garage structure, added to the William J. Rutter Community Center record on 2026-09-20, is UCSF's own separate 'Block 21A -- Community Center Garage', distinct from the Rutter Center itself (21B), even though the two are physically connected (a real rooftop parking deck joined to the community center building by a walkway). Split into two records along a clean straight line following the Rutter Center's own real west wall (idealized from a 3-point digitizing jog to a straight 2-point edge) rather than the raw polygon difference, which left thin sliver artifacts at the seam. The Rutter Center record (21B) reverts to its original OpenStreetMap building footprint; the garage (21A, new record) is approximate -- DataSF's own Building Footprints dataset does not separate the two structures, so there is no official boundary between them.

item.title: Correction · CORRECTION to the prior 'block-by-block reconciliation' pass: the owner questioned why several plan blocks (6W/6E/7W/7E, 15A/15B, 18B) weren't visible on the rendered map, which prompted an actual satellite-imagery check of those specific areas rather than trusting the prior pass's own description of itself as exhaustive. 15A/15B/18B turned out to already be covered (the visually 'empty' area there is a real surface parking lot, not a missed building). But the 6W/6E/7W/7E area had two genuine, real, significant gaps the prior automated scan had not surfaced: MB360 (1200 4th St) -- a second, ~180m-separated volume of the already-tracked MB360 development (both 701 China Basin St and 1200 4th St are used for the same marketed 'MB360' community across apartment-listing sites) -- and Sister Lillian Murphy Community (671-691 China Basin St), a 152-unit affordable housing development by Mercy Housing, celebrated in an April 2022 City/Mayor event, not previously tracked at all. MB360 (1200 4th St)'s footprint originally overlapped the adjacent Mission Bay Kids' Park by 69 sq m -- trimmed to the non-overlapping remainder, same pattern as the Mission Walk/Arterra fix in the prior pass. This is a reminder that an automated footprint scan is only as complete as its own coverage-detection logic (which, as seen with the Uber and 400/410 China Basin false positives, can both over- and under-report); a direct visual spot-check against satellite imagery remains the most reliable verification and should have been part of the original reconciliation claim, not a follow-up prompted by the owner catching it.

item.title: Added · Mission Bay 7E/7W spot-check (prompted by the owner asking directly about that block): matched the plan's block '7E'/'7W' label position against real street geometry (both letters resolve to the same coarse real block, since no mapped street divides them) and found a real, previously untracked building on its own standalone Assessor lot (blklot 8711227, recorded 2012) -- the Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House, 540 Mission Bay Blvd North: a 5-story, 80-room nonprofit free lodging house for families of children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital, built 2016. Identified via the DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Roll API (property_location, use code, year built, welfare exemption all cross-checked) after OpenStreetMap/Overpass lookups failed to name it -- added only once that gave a citable address and name, not from proximity alone. A second candidate found the same way, at 1600 Owens St (blklot 8709020) near block 18A/18B, turned out to be a false lead: the DataSF Assessor tax-roll lookup that identified it as 'Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices' also revealed it was already tracked as a real parcel-joined status.csv row (added in an earlier pass with more detailed sourcing than this one found) -- check_geometry_quality.py --strict caught the 3,023 sq m overlap before it was committed, and the duplicate file was removed rather than left in. item.title: Added · Mission Bay Block 6E real-parcel find, prompted by the owner directly asking why the map only showed 7E and not 7W. Investigating that pushed a re-check of the plan-to-real-world transform's local accuracy: the label positions for 7E and 7W (fit from 6 control points clustered in the South campus core) drift enough this far out that the 7W label position actually lands inside a different, adjacent block's building -- 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East), a 142-unit TNDC affordable housing development (plus a manager's unit, mid-block mews of 12 townhomes/10 flats, groundbreaking anticipated in 2016 per SocketSite's Aug 2016 'about to break ground' item) that was genuinely untracked. Confirmed via its own standalone Assessor parcel (blklot 8711505) and DataSF's Historical Secured Property Tax Roll; DataSF's Building Footprints layer only captures small roof-edge fragments of this building (confirmed against satellite imagery), so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly rather than the incomplete footprint layer. Added as a real status.csv row, not an approximate trace. This is a concrete instance of the known limitation already logged for the PDF-transform approach: label positions this far from the control-point cluster cannot be trusted for identifying which real building a plan label refers to without an independent check (here, the DataSF Assessor tax-roll API) -- exactly the caveat under which the transform was adopted in the first place.

item.title: Added · Potrero Power Station photo pass with Mapillary enabled: of 366 candidates (27 Wikimedia Commons, 339 Mapillary), 2 survived triage (The Stack and Station A, recorded above). All 22 Potrero records lack a current photo; the Mapillary imagery near them was 79% from a single GoProMAX3M account already shown on Mission Rock and Pier 70 to carry mismatched location metadata (confirmed again here with the same Chinatown/Union Square content reused near multiple Potrero blocks), plus older 2015-2016 imagery from before the redevelopment's construction-start milestones. Two Commons photos of the Stack and Station A from a single February 2020 session, tagged to adjacent blocks by geosearch proximity, were the pass's only finds; the shot list shrank by 2 (110 to 108).

item.title: Added · Mission Bay photo pass with Mapillary enabled, the last of the four sites: of 1510 candidates (311 Wikimedia Commons, 1199 Mapillary), none survived triage. No GoProMAX3M-style mislabeled contributor turned up here; the dominant Mapillary sources (andrewsnow, richlv, lvl5, bhousel -- 2015-2019 OSM-style systematic mapping -- and the same reliable 2025 marker_geo/marker_geo1 road survey seen at Mission Rock and Potrero) are geographically consistent, but none gave a safely attributable current photo for the 13 dossier-backed records still lacking one. One marker_geo frame near the UCSF campus was nearly hosted on ucsf_helen_diller_cancer_research before its own legible signage read 'UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center' -- a different, related facility already covered under ucsf_mission_bay_hospital -- caught and rejected rather than hosted on either record. The 41 no-dossier Mission Bay records are unchanged; the shot list stays at 108 rows.
